title: The gray pixels are tunnel lining (replaces the 300-ant, one-frame card)
question: With every kind of ground in its own colour, over time: is the cyan -- the lining of every tunnel -- the grey you were asking about?
context_md:
You asked **"what are all the gray pixels in the image?"** on the 'one giant hole' card. **Replaces card 20260926T033823143Z-6faaf7**, which answered it at 300 ants on one frame. Per your note, this is **40 ants** that cannot breed, at **frames 0, 3,000, 6,000 and 12,000**, drawn twice from one run: as the game draws it, and with each kind of ground painted flat.

- **Cyan: tunnel lining.** Every cell an ant digs turns the soil around it into lining, so the tunnel stays open. Lining has its own greyer brown, so every tunnel reads as a line of grey grit. It is almost all of what is not plain soil.
- **Magenta: ants** (nearly black in the game).
- **Orange: dumped spoil.**
- **Yellow: loose soil above the old ground line.**
- **White: the painted nest strip.**

At this colony size almost nothing floats in the sky: 1 to 28 cells of dirt with no path to the floor across four seeds. The arch you saw hanging over the 300-ant nest grows with the crowd.

items.label: Each kind of ground in its own colour
items.caption: cyan lining, magenta ants, orange spoil, yellow loose soil above ground, white nest strip
